Chapter 1: Zensar Technologies – Company Overview

1.1  About Zensar Technologies

Zensar Technologies Limited is a leading global technology consulting and services organization with an engineering-led heritage, operating as an integral technology business of RPG Enterprises—one of India's prominent industrial conglomerates. Headquartered at the Zensar Kharadi Knowledge Park in Pune, Maharashtra, India, the company employs over 11,000 skilled associates across more than 30 strategic delivery hubs, innovation labs, and client executive centers worldwide.

The operational model of Zensar is driven by its foundational paradigm of Experience-Led Everything (ELE). ELE bridges human-centric experience design with modern cloud architectures, artificial intelligence, and advanced data engineering, enabling Fortune 500 enterprises and high-growth mid-market leaders to accelerate digital velocity, streamline operating models, and realize measurable business outcomes.

Zensar operates as a publicly traded company listed on the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE: ZENSARTECH) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE: 504067). It is subject to rigorous corporate governance standards, statutory audits, and regulatory disclosures mandated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

1.2  Company History and Background

Zensar Technologies possesses an established corporate heritage spanning more than half a century. Originating as a pioneer in computer hardware and computing systems in India, the organization progressively transformed into an international software development powerhouse, maintaining continuous public listing on Indian bourses for more than 50 years.

Throughout its technological evolution, Zensar has successfully adapted to major industry paradigm shifts: from early mainframe computing and client-server systems to enterprise internet solutions, software-as-a-service (SaaS) integrations, cloud-native transformations, and autonomous artificial intelligence.

Integration with RPG Enterprises provided the institutional capital, cross-industry relationships, and values-led leadership necessary to scale operations internationally. Over the decades, Zensar expanded through strategic organic growth and high-value mergers and acquisitions, continuously refreshing its capabilities to address emerging enterprise demands.

1.3  Vision, Purpose and Values

Zensar's organizational vision and corporate purpose are encapsulated in its unifying mission statement: 'Together, We Shape Experiences for Better Futures.' This vision asserts that technology serves a human purpose—empowering employees, elevating client brand experiences, enriching end-user journeys, and generating sustainable social value.

The operational values of the organization are codified in the 'Values in Motion' framework. These values govern the daily workplace conduct, architectural decisions, and performance evaluations of every associate:

1.4  Business Overview and Services

Zensar provides full-lifecycle digital engineering, consulting, and technology operations to enterprise clients across global markets. The service architecture is structured into five core solution practices:

1. Digital Experience & Product Engineering: Human-centered experience design, modern UI/UX design systems, omnichannel customer journey engineering, and bespoke software product engineering.
2. Advanced Cloud & Modern IT Infrastructure: Cloud advisory, multi-cloud migrations (Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform), cloud-native application architectures, microservices, and automated CI/CD DevOps pipelines.
3. Enterprise Applications & Digital SaaS: Implementation, modernization, and managed operations for market-leading enterprise suites, including Oracle Cloud Fusion (HRMS, Financials, SCM), Salesforce, SAP S/4HANA, and ServiceNow.
4. Data Engineering, Advanced Analytics & Artificial Intelligence: Scalable enterprise data fabrics, data lakes, modern BI dashboards, machine learning operations (MLOps), and enterprise Generative AI integrations.
5. Digital Foundation & Next-Gen Cybersecurity: Zero-trust cybersecurity architectures, automated security operations centers (SOC), endpoint protection, network infrastructure, and automated IT service desk management.

1.5  Global Presence and Office Locations

Zensar maintains an integrated global delivery model spanning over 30 strategic locations worldwide. This distributed footprint facilitates follow-the-sun engineering delivery, business continuity, and localized client collaboration:

• India Delivery Hubs: Pune (Global Headquarters at Zensar Kharadi Knowledge Park), Hyderabad (HITEC City), Bengaluru (Electronic City & Whitefield), Chennai (OMR / Guindy), Kolkata (Salt Lake Sector V), and Mumbai.
• North America Hubs: United States corporate delivery hubs in Princeton (New Jersey), San Jose (California), Dallas (Texas), Chicago (Illinois), and regional consulting presences.
• United Kingdom & Europe Hubs: Reading and London offices supporting UK financial, retail, and public sector clients, alongside delivery nodes in Continental Europe.
• South Africa Delivery Centers: Regional headquarters in Johannesburg and Cape Town, operating as a certified Top Employer supporting major African financial and telecommunication enterprises.
• Asia-Pacific Hubs: Singapore and Australia delivery presences providing localized engineering support.

1.6  Organizational Structure

Zensar's organizational governance operates through a structured executive leadership council led by the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director (CEO & MD), supported by practice leadership and corporate shared services:

• Global Delivery & Practice Leadership: Governing industry-specific Business Units (BUs) and horizontal technology service lines.
• Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Organization: Governing financial planning, commercial contracting, investor relations, and statutory accounting (led by CFO Pulkit Bhandari).
• Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO) Organization: Governing talent acquisition, total rewards, HR operations, employee relations, learning & development, and culture transformation.
• Chief Information Officer (CIO) Organization: Governing enterprise IT, cybersecurity, internal applications (OneRPG, ZenFusion), infrastructure, and service desk operations.
• Global Sales & Marketing: Driving enterprise client partnerships, brand storytelling, and strategic analyst relations.

1.8  Company Milestones and Achievements

Zensar's consistent pursuit of operational excellence, employee satisfaction, and technological innovation is evidenced by prestigious national and international recognitions:

• Great Place to Work® 2026: Zensar achieved Rank #6 in India's Best Companies to Work For® 2026 and clinched the #1 position nationwide in the IT Services sector (a major leap from #47 in the preceding evaluation cycle).
• Avtar & Seramount Workplace Excellence 2026: Awarded 'Best Companies - Hall of Fame' (for being featured consistently for 5+ years), 'Best Companies for Women in India' (BCWI), and 'Exemplars of Inclusion' under the Most Inclusive Companies Index (MICI).
• iNFHRA Platinum Awards: Conferred the Platinum Award for Leadership in ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) Excellence and workplace infrastructure.
• Brandon Hall Group Excellence Awards: Multiple Gold and Platinum awards recognizing outstanding achievement in Human Capital Management, talent programs, and learning strategy.
• Training APEX / Training MVP: Honored as a winner for five consecutive years by Training Magazine for world-class enterprise learning and capability-building programs.
• Hermes Creative Awards: Platinum Award honoring excellence in corporate communication, creative storytelling, and employer brand engagement.
• Top Employer South Africa: Four-time certified Top Employer in South Africa by the Top Employers Institute, recognizing people practices and workplace environment.
• Strategic Acquisition: Full acquisition of BridgeView Life Sciences LLC (announced July 18, 2024), expanding consultative life sciences and pharmaceutical domain capability in the US.
• Innovation Hubs & Partnerships: Inauguration of the Gaming Experience Lab (GXL) in Pune; launch of Old Mutual Limited's Global Capability Hub (GCH); top 10 finish in Guidewire DEVHack 2025; and awards at the GenAI Conclave 2025.

Chapter 2: Zensar Culture, Values and Workplace Conduct

2.1  Workplace Culture

Zensar fosters an open, collaborative, and merit-based workplace culture rooted in trust, innovation, and psychological safety. Associates are encouraged to challenge conventional approaches, author innovative solutions, and collaborate across functional disciplines without hierarchical barriers.

Cultural cohesion is nurtured through company-wide platforms and celebrations, including Innovation Day, Values in Motion recognition spotlights, Hackathons, town halls with executive leadership, and Happiness Corner celebrations. This vibrant culture directly contributed to Zensar being recognized as #6 in India's Best Companies to Work For® 2026.

2.2  Code of Conduct and Ethics

The Zensar Code of Conduct constitutes the definitive ethical operating framework for all associates, trainees, contractors, and business partners. It mandates strict adherence to local and international legal statutes, professional integrity, and uncompromised ethical principles.

Core tenets require absolute truthfulness in business communications, accurate time and expense reporting, zero tolerance for fraud or accounting irregularities, protection of corporate and client assets, and fair treatment of all stakeholders. Violations of the Code are investigated by the Ethics Committee and carry strict disciplinary consequences up to termination.

2.3  Professional Behaviour

Every associate is expected to embody professionalism in all client, partner, and colleague interactions. Professionalism encompasses punctuality for scheduled meetings, constructive communication during technical disputes, honoring sprint commitments, and maintaining emotional composure.

Dress Code: Business casual attire is the standard across Zensar campuses (Monday through Friday). Formal business attire is required for in-person client briefings, executive meetings, and client-site deployments.

2.4  Integrity and Conflict of Interest

Associates must avoid situations where personal, commercial, or family interests conflict with the legitimate business interests of Zensar Technologies. Associates must never use corporate assets, client data, proprietary software, or working hours for personal commercial gain.

Outside Employment & Directorships: Holding secondary employment, moonlighting, freelance contracting, or operating competing commercial businesses while employed at Zensar is strictly prohibited. Outside business activities or board appointments require formal written approval from the Legal and Compliance Department.

Anti-Bribery & Corruption: Offering, promising, soliciting, or accepting bribes, kickbacks, or improper commercial inducements is strictly forbidden under corporate policy and international anti-bribery statutes (such as the UK Bribery Act and the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act). Modest business gifts or hospitality must strictly comply with corporate threshold guidelines.

2.5  Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) are intrinsic pillars of Zensar's organizational strength. Recognitions from Avtar & Seramount—including 'Best Companies for Women in India' (BCWI), 'Exemplars of Inclusion' under the Most Inclusive Companies Index (MICI), and Hall of Fame honors—affirm Zensar's commitment to gender equity and cultural inclusion.

DEI initiatives include proactive gender-balanced recruitment pipelines, structured leadership mentoring for women leaders, accessibility infrastructure for persons with disabilities, sensitization workshops, and supportive family leave policies.

2.6  Respectful Workplace

Zensar is committed to providing a secure, productive, and respectful work environment that affirms human dignity. Bullying, intimidation, derogatory slurs, abusive language, psychological harassment, and belittling remarks are completely unacceptable.

Managers are specifically accountable for maintaining team psychological safety, resolving interpersonal friction objectively, and ensuring every associate feels valued and heard.

2.7  Prevention of Harassment and Discrimination

Zensar strictly enforces its policy on the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) in full compliance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, and global anti-harassment regulations. The policy protects women employees, interns, project trainees, contract workers, and visitors across all campuses, client locations, and work-related virtual events.

Internal Complaints Committee (ICC): Zensar has constituted a legally compliant Internal Complaints Committee headed by senior women leaders, employee representatives, and an independent external NGO specialist. The ICC is invested with statutory authority to investigate complaints thoroughly, objectively, and confidentially.

Reporting Channels & Protection: Complaints must be addressed directly to POSH@zensar.com, the relevant HRBP, or the reporting manager. Inquiries are conducted under strict confidentiality. Retaliation against any individual reporting in good faith is strictly prohibited and results in immediate termination of employment.

2.8  Confidentiality and Professional Responsibility

During employment, associates have access to confidential enterprise data, source code repositories, client system designs, customer PII, commercial contracts, and pricing models. Preserving the confidentiality of this data is a binding legal duty.

Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs): Associates sign binding non-disclosure agreements upon joining. Proprietary code, architectural diagrams, customer lists, and financial reports must never be disclosed to third parties, forwarded to personal email accounts, or shared on external public social media forums. NDA obligations remain legally enforceable even after separation from Zensar.

2.9  Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability

Zensar's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) agenda is executed through the RPG Foundation and internal volunteer networks. Key initiatives focus on digital literacy programs for underserved communities, STEM education for young girls, environmental conservation, and local community health.

Sustainability Recognition: Zensar has earned the iNFHRA Platinum Award for ESG Excellence. The company actively implements green campus operations, including solar energy installations, rainwater harvesting, zero-waste-to-landfill certifications, and comprehensive elimination of single-use plastics across office campuses.

Chapter 3: Common HR and Workplace Guidelines

3.1  Working Hours

Zensar operates on business schedules designed to support client delivery agreements, international timezone overlaps, and agile team collaboration. Standard business hours typically encompass 9 hours per working day (including a 1-hour interval for lunch and refreshments), totaling 45 hours weekly, Monday through Friday.

Project-specific working hours, core team overlap windows (e.g., mandatory overlap hours with US or UK client teams), and sprint stand-up schedules are defined by individual project managers and delivery leads.

Status: Requires Verification – Official daily working hours and flexible band parameters should be confirmed with the respective practice HRBP.

3.2  Attendance Guidelines

Physical attendance at Zensar facilities is tracked electronically through smart RFID access cards and automated turnstiles. Associates must swipe their valid company badge upon entering and exiting campus gates and secure development floors.

Access cards are strictly non-transferable. Swiping an access card for an absent colleague ('buddy punching') is considered gross misconduct subject to formal disciplinary action. Electronic swipe records are reconciled with monthly timesheet entries and leave ledgers.

3.3  Shift Guidelines

Teams providing 24/7 cloud management, infrastructure support, or continuous operational monitoring operate on rotating shift schedules. Shift allocations, rotation cycles, and handover protocols are coordinated by project leads.

Status: Information Not Found – Official shift allowance slabs, night shift cab transport eligibility, and rotational shift rosters require confirmation from Practice HR Operations.

3.4  Work-from-Office and Work-from-Home Guidelines

Zensar implements a structured hybrid operating model combining in-person campus collaboration with remote flexibility. Hybrid eligibility and mandatory in-office day requirements are established by project leadership based on client contract terms and security compliance.

Associates approved for hybrid or remote working must maintain a dedicated, ergonomic home workspace, ensure reliable high-speed broadband, connect through the corporate VPN, remain reachable during core hours on Microsoft Teams, and safeguard client confidentiality.

3.5  Holiday Calendar

Zensar publishes an official corporate holiday calendar annually for each regional office location. Indian delivery centers observe 10 to 11 public and festival holidays annually, combining mandatory national holidays with state-specific festival observances.

Below is the verified corporate holiday schedule across key Indian delivery locations:

Multi-Location Statutory and Festive Holiday Structure: Zensar Technologies declares an official annual holiday calendar tailored to statutory regulations and regional cultural observances across its Indian delivery locations. Depending on the campus (Pune HQ, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Mumbai), associates observe between 10 and 12 declared mandatory holidays per calendar year. Common mandatory national holidays observed uniformly across all Indian centers include Republic Day (26th January), Independence Day (15th August), and Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October). Regional festive holidays are aligned with state government notifications, such as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti, Gudhi Padwa, Maharashtra Day, Ganesh Chaturthi, and Diwali (Laxmi Pujan & Balipratipada) in Pune; Ugadi, Kannada Rajyotsava, and Ayudha Puja in Bangalore; Sankranti, Ugadi, and Bonalu in Hyderabad; and Pongal, Tamil New Year, and Ayutha Pooja in Chennai.

Restricted, Floating, and Optional Holidays: In addition to mandatory location-specific holidays, Zensar provides an Optional / Floating Holiday benefit. Eligible associates may elect one to two optional holidays per calendar year from a pre-approved restricted holiday roster published on the Zenith portal. Optional holidays accommodate diverse cultural, spiritual, and personal observances. Applications for optional holidays must be submitted through Zenith Self-Service at least two weeks in advance and are subject to project delivery coverage and managerial concurrence.

Client and Shift-Aligned Project Calendars: Associates assigned to international client accounts, dedicated Global Delivery Centers, or 24x7 mission-critical operations may follow client-specific working calendars (e.g., US Federal, UK Bank, or Australian public holidays) rather than local Indian holiday schedules. In such operational setups, working on a local declared holiday entitles the associate to either compensatory off (Comp-Off) or alternative holiday scheduling, subject to PMO authorization and client contract governance.

3.6  Common Workplace Rules

Physical Security: All associates must carry and display their official Zensar ID badge while on company property. Tailgating through access turnstiles is strictly prohibited. External visitors must be registered at security gates and escorted by authorized hosts.

Restricted Items & Substance Ban: Personal heavy luggage, unauthorized external storage drives, and cameras are restricted in secure delivery bays. Smoking, alcohol consumption, vaping, and possession of illicit substances are strictly prohibited across all campuses.

Recording Prohibition: Unauthorized photography, audio recording, or video recording inside office buildings and development floors is strictly forbidden.

3.7  General HR Support Procedures

HR support at Zensar is delivered through an integrated multi-tier service framework accessible via OneRPG:

• Tier 1 - Self-Service: Knowledge bases, FAQs, and automated policy guides on OneRPG > Policies & Guidelines and ZenPolicies.
• Tier 2 - HR Service Desk / Talent@Zensar: Raising digital inquiries for employment letters, background checks, policy clarifications, or leave adjustments via Talent@Zensar > Ask a Question or hrservices@zensar.com.
• Tier 3 - People Partners / HRBPs: Dedicated HR Business Partners assigned to individual business units for career development, grievance mediation, and organizational transitions.

Chapter 4: Timesheet and Work Reporting

4.1  Timesheet Process

Accurate daily time recording is an essential operational obligation for all associates at Zensar. Timesheets provide the foundational data for client project billing, payroll verification, capacity planning, and statutory audit compliance.

Timesheet Entry Portal: Associates submit time records electronically via the enterprise Timesheet Portal, accessible directly at https://timesheet.zensar.com/login or via OneRPG > My Applications > Timesheet Portal. Talent@Zensar also provides an integrated timesheet entry route. Sign in using corporate email credentials and complete Microsoft Authenticator verification if prompted.

Data Fields: For each working day, associates log in, select the date, choose the assigned project code, select the specific task type (e.g., Development, Testing, Bug Fixing, Architectural Design, Meeting), enter hours worked, indicate billability status, and provide concise task comments.

4.2  Timesheet Submission

Timesheets must be submitted on a weekly basis, accounting for standard daily working hours across authorized project codes or approved leave codes. Once hours are entered, associates review the summary and click 'Confirm & Submit'. The timesheet status immediately changes to 'Submitted'.

Replicate Timesheet Feature: The portal features a productivity tool allowing associates on repetitive tasks to copy entries: click 'Replicate Timesheet', select a previously approved or submitted timesheet date as the source, select destination dates, choose 'Replicate', and verify the resulting entries before final confirmation.

4.3  Submission Deadlines

Timesheets must be submitted weekly before the designated cut-off (typically Friday evening or Monday morning before 10:00 AM IST, depending on project SLA cut-offs). Prompt submission is essential for weekly client billing and monthly payroll reconciliation.

Strict 10-Working-Day Lookback Window: The Zensar timesheet system strictly enforces an automated rule: associates may enter or adjust timesheet entries for only the preceding 10 working days. Any time logging beyond the 10-day lookback window is permanently locked by the system.

4.4  Approval Process

Submitted timesheets are automatically routed to the designated Project Manager (PM) or Reporting Manager for electronic review and approval in the portal.

Managers verify that logged effort matches sprint deliverables, task allocations, and approved client billing codes. If a discrepancy exists, the timesheet is rejected with reviewer comments and returned to the associate for immediate correction and resubmission.

4.5  Timesheet Corrections

If an associate fails to submit timesheets within the authorized 10-day lookback window, the missing period is classified by the system as unauthorized absence. The automated HR system executes a strict progressive leave deduction hierarchy:

1. Flexi Leave (FL) Deduction: Missing working days are first automatically deducted from the associate's available Flexi Leave balance.
2. Privileged Leave (PL) Deduction: If Flexi Leave is exhausted, missing days are deducted from the accumulated Privileged Leave balance.
3. Loss of Pay (LOP): If both leave balances are exhausted, the unlogged days result in formal Loss of Pay (salary deduction) during the subsequent payroll cycle.

To request an exceptional correction within the allowable period, the associate must submit an attendance correction request through the portal with manager justification.

4.6  Work Reporting Expectations

In addition to timesheet entry, associates participate in structured project work reporting workflows, including daily 15-minute stand-up ceremonies, sprint reviews, and weekly status reports.

Associates must report blockers, technical dependencies, and schedule variances proactively to their leads, ensuring complete visibility across project delivery chains.

Chapter 5: IT, Information Security and Data Protection

5.1  IT Usage Policies

Zensar provides IT equipment, software licenses, network bandwidth, and email services solely for legitimate business operations. All hardware, software, communications, and data stored on company infrastructure remain the exclusive property of Zensar Technologies.

Prohibited Computing Activities: Installing unauthorized third-party software, peer-to-peer file sharing applications, cryptocurrency mining software, personal gaming software, or hacking utilities is strictly prohibited. Network traffic is monitored and audited to maintain cybersecurity standards.

5.2  Password and Authentication Guidelines

Zensar enforces stringent password complexity standards across all enterprise domains. First-time joiners receive temporary credentials that must be changed immediately upon initial login through the enterprise self-service portal.

ADSelfService Plus Portal: All password management, initial account enrollment, security question configuration, and self-service password resets are performed via https://adselfservice.zensar.com. Passwords must meet enterprise complexity criteria (minimum 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special symbols) and must not be shared or reused across accounts.

ADSelfService Plus Identity Governance: All Zensar enterprise accounts are governed through the centralized ADSelfService Plus identity management framework (accessible at https://adselfservice.zensar.com). Upon receiving initial temporary credentials from the Talent Acquisition or Onboarding Operations team, associates are required to perform their initial system login through this portal. Initial enrollment establishes self-service account recovery capabilities and configures mandatory multi-channel identity verification.

42-Day Password Expiry Lifecycle: Enterprise domain passwords remain valid for exactly forty-two (42) calendar days. Automated notification emails are dispatched to the associate's corporate inbox starting 14 days, 7 days, and 3 days prior to expiration. The password configured via ADSelfService operates as a unified Single Sign-On (SSO) credential, controlling access to corporate Exchange webmail, OneRPG SharePoint intranet, Talent@Zensar (T@Z), Zenith ERP, ServiceNow/IS Service Desk, and Windows network domain logon.

Mandatory Profile Enrollment Format: During enrollment, associates must register two critical recovery channels: (1) Primary Mobile Number: Must be inputted in international format without symbols, spaces, or plus signs (e.g., standard Indian format is 919890989099; entering +91 or leading zeroes will invalidate SMS gateway delivery); (2) Personal Email Account: A non-Zensar external email address (e.g., Gmail, Outlook) to receive One-Time Passwords (OTPs) when corporate access is locked or expired; and (3) Security Challenge Questions: Configuration of three secret challenge questions.

Four Authorized Password Reset Channels: In the event of password expiration, account lockout, or forgotten credentials, associates must utilize one of four sanctioned reset channels: (a) Direct Web Portal: Access https://adselfservice.zensar.com from any internet-connected desktop or smartphone; (b) Windows Logon Screen: Click the 'Reset Password / Unlock Account' hyperlink embedded on the corporate Windows logon screen; (c) Cisco Cloud VPN + Ctrl+Alt+Del: While connected to the corporate VPN network, press Ctrl+Alt+Del and select 'Change a password' to simultaneously synchronize Active Directory and local cached credentials; or (d) Emergency IT Helpdesk: Transmit an urgent ticket request from the registered personal email ID with managerial approval to IThelpdesk@zensar.com.

5.3  Multi-Factor Authentication

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is mandatory for accessing all Zensar enterprise systems, including Microsoft 365, Outlook email, OneRPG intranet, single sign-on (SSO) portals, and VPN connections.

MFA Setup Procedure: Associates download the Microsoft Authenticator app on their mobile phone, link it to their corporate account via QR code during initial setup, and approve push notifications or enter time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) when logging in from new devices or external networks.

Azure AD Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Implementation: Zensar enforces mandatory Multi-Factor Authentication across Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) for all enterprise identities. MFA enrollment is enforced on day one before an associate can access Microsoft 365 cloud workloads, corporate email (Exchange Online), Microsoft Teams, SharePoint/OneRPG, or cloud SaaS applications.

Step-by-Step Microsoft Authenticator Configuration: Associates must complete MFA pairing by navigating to https://aka.ms/mfasetup via a desktop browser. The primary and recommended authentication method is the Microsoft Authenticator Application (available free on Apple App Store and Google Play Store). During setup, associates select 'Work or school account', scan the dynamic QR code presented on the browser, and complete the interactive Number Matching challenge by typing the two-digit numeric code displayed on the screen into the phone prompt.

Secondary Fallback Authentication: In addition to the mobile app push notification, associates must register a secondary backup authentication mechanism. This is configured as SMS One-Time Password (OTP) or automated phone call verification to the employee's registered mobile number. The backup method ensures uninterrupted access when traveling or operating in areas with limited mobile data connectivity.

Zero-Trust MFA Security Rules: Associates must never approve an MFA push notification that they did not actively initiate. Approving unexpected prompts poses severe security risks and constitutes a violation of Information Security Policy. Any unexpected prompt must be rejected immediately by tapping 'No, it's not me', and reported to is.servicedesk@zensar.com.

5.4  Company Device Usage

Company-issued laptops and workstations must be enrolled in Microsoft Intune Mobile Device Management (MDM). Intune maintains security compliance, deploys critical patches, enforces BitLocker disk encryption, and enables remote data wipe capabilities if a device is lost or stolen.

Microsoft Intune Work Profile: When accessing corporate email or Teams from mobile devices, associates must install the Microsoft Intune Company Portal, which creates an encrypted, isolated 'Work Profile'. Corporate data and applications remain separated from personal apps, photos, and messages.

Microsoft Intune Mobile Device Management (MDM) & Mobile Application Management (MAM): Zensar utilizes Microsoft Intune endpoint management to secure corporate communications on mobile devices (BYOD - Bring Your Own Device). Any associate wishing to access corporate email, calendar, Microsoft Teams, or OneDrive on personal iOS or Android devices must enroll through the Microsoft Intune Company Portal application.

Android Work Profile Containerization: On Android devices, Intune establishes an isolated 'Android Work Profile'. Corporate applications (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Edge) reside entirely within this encrypted container, identified by a distinctive briefcase icon. Corporate security policies are strictly sandboxed within the work profile; Zensar IT administrators have zero visibility into personal applications, personal photos, personal browsing history, WhatsApp messages, or personal emails.

Mobile Security Compliance Mandates: Enrolled mobile devices must comply with core security baselines: (1) Minimum 6-digit complex numeric PIN or alphanumeric device unlock password; (2) Biometric authentication (fingerprint / Face ID) permitted to unlock the work container; (3) Inactivity auto-lock set to 15 minutes or less; (4) Device storage encryption enabled; and (5) Strict prohibition of rooted or jailbroken devices, which are automatically blocked from accessing corporate resources.

Selective Enterprise Remote Wipe: If an enrolled personal smartphone is lost, stolen, or when an associate separates from Zensar, TIMS executes a 'Selective Enterprise Wipe'. This action remotely erases only corporate data, work emails, and work container files, leaving personal photos, personal apps, and personal device settings completely untouched.

5.5  VPN and Network Access

Secure remote access to Zensar's internal development networks, client staging environments, and restricted repositories requires an authenticated Virtual Private Network (VPN) connection. Zensar deploys enterprise VPN clients configured with MFA.

Associates must never connect to company VPNs from unsecured public Wi-Fi networks (e.g., airports, cafes) without verifying network authenticity. VPN connections must be terminated when remote access to internal resources is no longer required.

Cisco AnyConnect Cloud-Based Secure Remote Access: Remote connectivity to Zensar's corporate network and internal applications is established using Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client connected to cloud-based Cisco Security Service Edge (SSE) infrastructure.

Step-by-Step VPN Connection Procedure: (1) Launch the installed Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client on the corporate laptop; (2) In the connection address field, enter the official cloud gateway URL: 6d7c.vpn.sse.cisco.com and click 'Connect'; (3) In the authentication pop-up window, ensure the VPN profile is set to 'ZENSAR-RAVPN'; (4) Enter your full Zensar email ID and domain network password; (5) Complete the Microsoft Authenticator MFA push verification prompt on your mobile device; and (6) Verify the connection status shows 'Connected to 6d7c.vpn.sse.cisco.com'.

Mandatory Daily Connection for Remote / WFH Associates: Associates working under hybrid or Work-From-Home arrangements are strongly required to connect their corporate laptops to Cisco Cloud VPN at least once daily during business hours. Daily VPN connectivity ensures seamless background reception of critical Windows operating system security patches, McAfee / Microsoft Defender antivirus definition updates, SCCM endpoint compliance scripts, and domain credential synchronization.

5.6  Information Security

Information Security (InfoSec) at Zensar is certified under ISO/IEC 27001 standards and strict risk management frameworks. Digital information assets are classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Strictly Confidential.

Clean Desk and Clear Screen Policy: Associates must lock their workstation screens (Windows Key + L) whenever stepping away from their desks. Printed documents containing confidential information must be retrieved immediately from printers and locked in designated storage.

5.7  Data Privacy and Protection

Zensar strictly complies with global data privacy regulations, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and HIPAA where applicable. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of employees, candidates, and client customers must be processed lawfully and securely.

PII must never be transmitted over unencrypted channels, stored on unauthorized personal USB drives, or exported to personal cloud storage (e.g., Google Drive, Dropbox).

5.8  Phishing and Security Awareness

Phishing attacks represent a major threat to enterprise security. Zensar conducts periodic, simulated phishing campaigns to evaluate organizational awareness and educate associates on emerging threat vectors.

Associates must scrutinize sender email addresses, avoid clicking unsolicited links or opening unverified attachments, and never enter corporate credentials into external forms. Suspicious emails should be reported immediately using the 'Report Phishing' button in Outlook.

5.9  Security Incident Reporting

Any suspected cybersecurity incident, lost or stolen laptop, malware infection, unauthorized access attempt, or inadvertent data breach must be reported immediately to the Information Security Incident Response Team.

Reporting Channels: Contact the IT Helpdesk at IThelpdesk@zensar.com or raise an emergency ticket via the IS Service Desk Portal within 1 hour of identifying the incident. Prompt reporting mitigates enterprise liability and enables rapid threat containment.

Chapter 6: Communication and Collaboration

6.1  Email Guidelines

Corporate Microsoft Outlook email is Zensar's official channel for formal business communication, client interactions, contractual agreements, and administrative notices.

Associates must maintain professional email standards: clear and descriptive subject lines, concise and grammatically correct body text, appropriate use of CC and BCC, and the standard corporate email signature containing official designation, contact details, and confidentiality disclaimer.

6.2  Microsoft Teams

Microsoft Teams is Zensar's enterprise platform for real-time collaboration, instant messaging, audio/video conferencing, and document co-authoring. Teams enables agile communication across distributed global locations.

Team channels should be established for projects, client accounts, and functional practice areas. Important project decisions made in chat should be formally documented in project repositories or follow-up email summaries.

6.3  Meeting Etiquette

Professional meeting conduct is essential for productive collaboration. Organizers must provide clear meeting agendas, attach relevant pre-reading materials, and schedule meetings within standard business hours respecting cross-timezone participants.

Chapter 8: IT Helpdesk and Support

8.1  IT Helpdesk Process

The Zensar Information Systems (IS) Service Desk serves as the central point of contact for all technical issues, hardware failures, application access requests, and infrastructure support.

The Helpdesk operates on an automated ITIL-aligned service management framework, categorizing issues by severity, assigning tracking numbers, and routing tickets to specialized engineering teams based on defined SLAs.

Access Gateways: Navigate to OneRPG > My Applications > IS Service Desk Portal or visit https://servicedesk.zensar.com directly. Emails can also be routed to IThelpdesk@zensar.com.

IS Service Desk Enterprise Platform: All IT incidents, hardware faults, software requests, and enterprise access requisitions are managed through the centralized Information Services (IS) Service Desk, accessible via OneRPG > My Applications > IS Service Desk (https://servicedesk.zensar.com).

24-Hour Account Synchronization Delay Notice: For newly onboarded associates and interns, directory identity synchronization between Active Directory and ServiceNow / IS Service Desk requires up to twenty-four (24) hours following network ID creation. During this initial 24-hour synchronization window, new hires encountering urgent setup blocks should contact the TIMS desk via telephone or have their onboarding buddy/mentor log a ticket on their behalf.

8.2  Ticket Creation

To raise an IT support request, associates follow a structured self-service procedure on the intranet:

1. Access Portal: Navigate to OneRPG > My Applications > IS Service Desk Portal or https://servicedesk.zensar.com.
2. Select Request Type: Click on 'I Am Facing An Issue' (Incident) or 'I Need Something' (Service Request).
3. Categorize Issue: Select the appropriate category (e.g., Hardware, Software, Email, VPN, Network, Permissions). For laptop/desktop issues, select 'TIMS - Desktop Laptop Management Service'.
4. Provide Details: Enter a concise subject line, a detailed description of the error, step-by-step reproduction steps, and attach error screenshots or system logs.
5. Submit and Track: Submit the ticket, note the generated Ticket ID, and track resolution status through the portal.

Incident Logging vs Service Request: When accessing the IS Service Desk portal, users choose between two core pathways: (1) 'I am facing an issue' (Incident Ticket - logged for service disruptions, system crashes, network failures, or broken hardware); and (2) 'Make a Request' / '+' Icon (Service Request - logged for hardware allocation, software licenses, privilege access, or network configuration changes).

Categorization Taxonomy: To ensure immediate routing to the correct technical support queue, users must select the accurate category: (a) Laptop / Desktop hardware or OS issues: Select 'TIMS – Desktop Laptop Management Service'; (b) Timesheet portal issues: Select 'Talent@zensar'; (c) HRMS / Personal data issues: Select 'Oracle Fusion HCM Support'; (d) Network, Wi-Fi, or VPN issues: Select 'Network Infrastructure Services'; and (e) Enterprise messaging: Select 'O365 / Exchange Services'. Users must attach screenshots of error dialogs and provide corporate asset tags to accelerate resolution.

8.3  Hardware Support

Hardware support engineers provide diagnostic, repair, and replacement services for company laptops, monitors, power adapters, keyboards, and peripheral accessories.

If a laptop encounters hardware failure (e.g., battery degradation, screen malfunction, SSD failure), associates can bring the device to the on-campus IT walk-in desk or raise an emergency ticket for remote courier pickup if operating in an authorized remote capacity.

8.4  Software Installation and Access

Standard development utilities, licensed software suites (e.g., IDEs, databases, productivity tools), and enterprise applications are installed through approved IT software repositories or deployed automatically via Microsoft Intune.

Requests for non-standard software licenses or elevated permissions require formal project manager justification and manager approval in the IS Service Desk system prior to installation.

eForms Workflow Automation Platform: Requisition of non-standard software licenses, physical hardware infrastructure, and administrative permissions is strictly governed through the eForms portal (accessible at https://eforms.zensar.com or OneRPG > My Applications > eForms). The eForms system enforces automated governance, audit compliance, and managerial approval hierarchies.

Core eForms Service Modules: (1) Infrastructure Request Form: Utilized to request supplementary IT hardware, external monitors, docking stations, peripheral accessories, or laptop upgrades; (2) Additional Software Request Form: Utilized to request commercial developer software, IDE licenses (e.g., JetBrains IntelliJ, Visual Studio Professional, specialized database utilities), and licensed enterprise software not present in the self-service Software Center; and (3) Privilege Request Form: Utilized to request temporary, time-bound local administrative rights on developer laptops for specialized testing or compiler configuration.

End-to-End Approval Lifecycle: Once an eForm is submitted, the automated workflow routes through the associate's Reporting Manager -> Project Delivery Head -> IT Information Security (for privilege/software compliance) -> TIMS Fulfillment Team. Users can track real-time approval status under the 'My Requests' tab with state indicators (Pending Approval, Approved, In Progress, Fulfilled, Rejected).

Ans: Notify your project manager/lead as early as possible via email or Teams, and submit a medical leave request in MyLeaves upon resuming duties. A medical certificate is required for absences exceeding 3 consecutive days.
